messages:
maria: Quick sync — overnight batch failures: ~20% job exits due to GPU preemptions in us-west1. Looks like a single SKU (g5.12x) got hammered and a lot of pods were heavily binpacked on it. We lost KV-cache prefixes and saw long restart delays.

jon: Any logs or node events?

maria: kubectl describe pod ... shows:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason       Age   From               Message
  ----     ------       ----  ----               -------
  Warning  NodeLost     2m    kubelet, ip-...   Node was terminated: PreemptibleInstance
```
Also saw short 503 windows from model servers while rescheduling.

lee: Two quick reactions that won't require infra churn: 
- lower binpack density for spot lanes (target 60-70% GPU packing) so each eviction affects fewer pods
- add topologySpreadConstraints across instance "families" to avoid family-correlated preemptions (don't co-locate all replicas on same family)

sasha: Checkpointing: bump ckpt frequency to ~5m for background training. For inference: implement graceful fallback routing to on-demand pool or route to a quantized variant when nodeLoss detected.

praveen: On perf vs price: A100/H100 give best throughput but spot capacity is smaller and often correlated across hosts. T4/GPU4 variants are cheaper and more numerous but lower perf. My suggested 3-tier pool strategy:
- ha-pool: on-demand / reserved for latency-sensitive serving (pin large models)
- mixed-spot: diversified instance-family mix with lower binpack density + eviction-aware scheduling
- background-spot: cheapest instances, aggressive checkpointing and longer job windows

jon: How do we implement "eviction-aware scheduling" without a huge custom rewrite?

lee: Add an "interruptibility_score" node label computed from recent eviction history and price signals (0-100). Use a lightweight scheduling plugin that adds score into priority calculation. Also prefer soft nodeAffinity by family and topologySpread. Pseudocode snippet:
```
nodeAffinity:
  preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
  - weight: 50
    preference:
      matchExpressions:
      - key: gpu.family
        operator: In
        values: [a100, h100, g5, t4]
```
That keeps scheduler behavior simple but biases placements to diversify.

maria: Ops ask: run a small experiment this afternoon. Plan:
1) Lower binpack target for mixed-spot from 85% -> 65%
2) Add topologySpread on gpu.family as soft constraint
3) Increase checkpoint frequency for batch from 15m -> 5m
4) Add 10% warm buffer in mixed-spot autoscaler

sasha: I'll add an alert: if spot-eviction-rate > 5% over a 10m window -> auto rollback pack density and spin up ha-pool capacity.

jon: lgtm. If the experiment stabilizes us-west1 we can replicate config to eu-west1 next week.

maria: Thanks — I'll write the short runbook and kick off the experiment at 15:30 PT. Ping me if you want in. :thumbsup:
